To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the observation of hand actions interferes with the sensory processing of the hand.
‘Action observation (hand movements, passive touch) modulates the cortical response to a somatic stimulation of the hand.’
the observation of hand actions interferes with somatosensory cortex processing of hand sensations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural mechanisms of the perception of action.
how the human brain processes information about actions performed by others.
understanding how action observation affects somatosensory perception.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the somatosensensory system is modulated by the observation of actions, but not by the observation of static objects.
the effect is not a direct one of the action on the sensory cortex, rather it appears to be a result of the attentional focus being on the observed action and the hand being in the visual field.
the somatosensy cortex is involved in action execution and observation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
action observation modulates the response to somatosensory stimuli.
action observation and action execution share a common cortical network and that this network is sensitive to somatosensory inputs.
observation of a hand movement decreases the cortical response to somatosensory stimuli of the hand, whereas observation of a foot movement does not.
The main takeaway from our work is that
observation of a hand performing a task can interfere with the processing of sensory information from the same body part, a finding that may have implications for rehabilitation.
the observation of a hand action or being touched by a hand interferes with the sensory processing of the hand, a phenomenon that we termed as ‘sensory gating by action observation’.
action observation modulates the processing of somato-sensory information.
